description: Two-panel thermodynamic (Thermo-Calc) phase-fraction calculation for the Zr0.50 steel. Both panels plot phase fraction (dimensionless) against temperature (°C). The left (unlabelled) panel is a full-scale CALPHAD equilibrium plot, y = 0.0-1.0, x = 500-1000 °C, with four curves named by an in-panel legend: FCC (red), ZrC (green), BCC (blue) and κ carbide (purple). FCC rises steeply from just above the 0.6 gridline at 500 °C, passes ~0.9 near 550 °C, reaches the 1.0 line at about 700 °C and stays flat to 1000 °C. BCC drops from just above the 0.2 gridline at 500 °C to zero at ~550 °C. κ carbide decreases from near the 0.1 gridline at 500 °C to zero at about 700 °C. The ZrC curve lies essentially on the zero line at this scale, so the right panel re-plots the ordinate over 0.000-0.010: there the green ZrC line is horizontal just below the 0.006 gridline near 900 °C and a blue line sits at 0.000. Together the two panels show that above ~700 °C the matrix is single-phase FCC carrying a small, temperature-insensitive ZrC fraction, consistent with the caption's ~0.6 % ZrC after annealing at 900 °C. No numeric data labels are printed; values are read against gridlines.
measured_quantities: ZrC precipitate phase fraction (dimensionless, zoomed 0.000-0.010 range)

observations.observation: The left panel's legend names four phases exactly as printed: 'FCC' (red), 'ZrC' (green), 'BCC' (blue), 'κ carbide' (purple).
On the full-scale plot the FCC fraction rises from just above the 0.6 gridline at 500 °C, to about the 0.9 gridline at 550 °C, and reaches 1.0 at roughly 700 °C, remaining at 1.0 up to 1000 °C.
The BCC phase fraction decreases from just above the 0.2 gridline at 500 °C to zero at approximately 550 °C.
The κ carbide phase fraction decreases from near the 0.1 gridline at 500 °C and reaches zero at about 700 °C.
At the 0.0-1.0 scale the ZrC curve is indistinguishable from zero, which is why a second panel re-plots the ordinate over 0.000-0.010.
In the zoomed right panel the ZrC (green) fraction is horizontal and just below the 0.006 gridline over the plotted range around 900 °C, while a blue line lies exactly at 0.000.
The figure caption states that this is a thermodynamic phase fraction calculation for the Zr0.50 steel performed with Thermo-Calc software.
The citing text states that the fraction of ZrC particles is about 0.6 % after annealing at 900 °C, i.e. a phase fraction of roughly 0.006.
The citing text states that the average size and fraction of ZrC carbides are 30 nm and 0.006, giving a calculated precipitation strengthening of 108 MPa.

The citing text states that Zr is mainly distributed in the FCC matrix of the annealed Zr0.50 steel except for ZrC precipitation, and that the ZrC fraction is highest in Zr0.50 compared with the Zr0 and Zr0.01 steels.
No numeric values are printed on either panel's curves; all fractions have to be read against the axis gridlines.
Both panels carry the y-axis label 'Phase fraction' and the x-axis label 'Temperature (°C)'; the zoomed panel shows only one x tick, labelled 900.

subfigures.description: Unlabelled full-scale CALPHAD plot of phase fraction (0.0-1.0) vs temperature (500-1000 °C) for Zr0.50 steel. Red FCC curve rises from just above 0.6 at 500 °C to 1.0 at about 700 °C and stays flat to 1000 °C; blue BCC falls from just above 0.2 at 500 °C to zero near 550 °C; purple κ carbide falls from ~0.1 at 500 °C to zero at about 700 °C; green ZrC runs flat essentially on the zero line.

Unlabelled zoomed plot with phase-fraction ordinate expanded to 0.000-0.010 and an x-axis tick labelled 900 (Temperature, °C). A green horizontal line lies just below the 0.006 gridline (ZrC) and a blue line lies at 0.000.

Right panel: only the 900 °C x-axis tick is labelled, so the full temperature range of the zoom is not specified
